title: Unity 1: Being Together
hook: The old postmark matters before the fragile letters ever leave the family table.
counterintuition: Unity is not friendliness. It is a We relationship made conscious through legitimate identity, family, or place before cooperation is requested.
tryThisNow: Before asking for help, write the real We that already exists. If the phrase sounds borrowed, flattering, or vague, do not use it.
keyTakeaway: Unity works when a legitimate shared identity is brought forward before the request, making cooperation feel like care for one of us.

breakdown.fastRead:
An archivist sets a yellowed envelope on the table and names the street both families left behind. Only then does she open the loan agreement for the fragile letters. The trust request now sits inside a shared origin, not across a counter.

Unity is deeper than liking. It is a real We, built from shared identity. Family and place cues can bring that bond forward before a request. The cue has to be earned. Fake closeness breaks the trust unity is meant to create.
breakdown.deepRead:
A county birth registry lies open under a clinic lamp. Three nursing applicants see their family names on the page before the shift roster appears. The doctor is not saying the job is easy. She is making place identity visible before asking people to serve the county that raised them.

We is a serious word.

Source support identifies unity as an additional principle of influence, distinct from the familiar six. A shared identity can increase acceptance, cooperation, liking, help, trust, and assent when it is brought forward before the ask. The first route uses cues tied to family and place.

That boundary matters. A shared hometown, family mark, campus doorway, clan greeting, or arrival map can create togetherness when it is real. A fake We can sound warm and still be theft.
breakdown.fullRead:
A repaired net lies across a dock crate while siblings argue about buying a new boat engine. The budget sheet is ready, but the adviser first asks each sibling to identify the net-mending mark their grandfather taught them. The mark is small. The shared identity is not.

This is unity by being together. The request is not, like me. It is, remember what we are part of. That difference separates unity from ordinary rapport. Rapport can make a person pleasant to hear. Unity can make a request feel like care for a shared body.

A developer asking elders to record pronunciations for a language app can play a child saying the clan greeting before showing the consent form. The greeting belongs to the group before it belongs to the app. A college officer can show the flooded doorway every graduate used as a first-year student before opening the gift field for repairs. The doorway says, this place held us.

Where is the real We, and who has the right to name it?

The risk is exploitation. Shared origin, family, and place are powerful because they reach below preference. Do not borrow them to smooth a request that mainly serves you. Do not invent closeness. Do not say family when the relationship is merely convenient.

Use unity only where the bond can survive being named aloud by the people inside it.

examples.title: Lea Names the Street on the Envelope

planSpec.audience: an archivist asking families to loan fragile letters
planSpec.stakes: whether shared origin is brought forward before the trust request
planSpec.requiredBeat: the archivist opens with the street name both families left behind before presenting the loan agreement

examples.scenario: A yellowed envelope with an old neighborhood postmark rests beside Lea’s loan agreement. At 3:30 p.m. in the archive reading room, Lea is the archivist deciding whether the shared street belongs before the loan agreement. The family is about to decide whether fragile letters can leave the apartment. Before she presents the form, Lea names the street both families left behind decades ago. The room changes because the request now begins inside shared origin, not institutional custody.
examples.whatToDo: Name the shared street from the postmark before showing the loan agreement. Let real origin carry the trust request.
examples.whyItMatters: The place cue creates a legitimate We. The family is not handing letters to a stranger first; they are speaking with someone tied to the same lost street.

examples.title: Thomas Opens the County Registry

planSpec.audience: a doctor asking nurses to return to their home county
planSpec.stakes: whether place identity makes the request feel like serving one’s own
planSpec.requiredBeat: the doctor points to the county birth registry where three applicants’ families appear before discussing shifts

examples.scenario: A county registry lies open under a clinic lamp while Thomas points to three family names before sliding over the shift roster. Nurses must decide whether returning home is a staffing sacrifice or service to their own county. The registry does not make night shifts easier. It makes place identity present before the roster becomes the whole conversation.
examples.whatToDo: Show the birth-registry names before the shift roster. Let place identity appear before the hard staffing ask.
examples.whyItMatters: The request is heard through belonging to the county, not through vacancy pressure alone. That is unity, not a staffing pitch.

examples.title: Helena Asks About the Net Mark

planSpec.audience: an adviser mediating siblings on boat investment
planSpec.stakes: whether family unity is active before the capital decision
planSpec.requiredBeat: the adviser has each sibling identify the net-mending mark taught by their grandfather before opening the budget

examples.scenario: A repaired net lies across a dock crate while Helena keeps the budget sheet closed. At 6:45 a.m. on the harbor dock, Helena is the family mediator deciding whether the repaired net should be named before the engine budget. “Who made this mark?” she asks. “Granddad,” one sibling says. “He showed all of us,” says another. They must decide whether to fund the boat engine, but Amelia has them identify the net repair mark before any number appears. The budget now enters a room where family unity is active.
examples.whatToDo: Ask each sibling to identify the shared net-mending mark before opening the budget sheet. Bring family identity forward first.
examples.whyItMatters: The investment becomes a decision by people who share a working inheritance. That does not settle the budget, but it changes the ground for cooperation.

examples.title: Ruth Plays the Child’s Clan Greeting

planSpec.audience: a developer asking elders to record pronunciations
planSpec.stakes: whether shared identity precedes technology concerns
planSpec.requiredBeat: the developer plays a child saying the clan greeting before showing the recording consent form

examples.scenario: A small recorder sits beside a handwritten greeting card as Ruth prepares the consent form. The elders are about to decide whether the language app feels useful or extractive. Before the form appears, she plays a child saying the clan greeting. Ruth must decide whether shared identity should be present before technology concerns take the first seat.
examples.whatToDo: Play the child’s clan greeting before showing the consent form. Then explain the recording terms plainly.
examples.whyItMatters: The greeting belongs to the elders’ We before it belongs to the app. It makes the request about continuity, not just technology.

examples.title: David Shows the Doorway Under Water

planSpec.audience: a college officer asking graduates to support flood repairs
planSpec.stakes: whether campus place cues create We before the donation page
planSpec.requiredBeat: the officer shows the flooded doorway everyone used as freshmen before the gift field

examples.scenario: A photo shows a stone campus doorway under floodwater beside David’s gift field and freshman directory. Before the photo, graduates treated the repair appeal like another annual fund email. After he shows the doorway everyone used as freshmen, the gift field changes. The ask still costs money, but the place cue creates a We around a shared threshold.
examples.whatToDo: Show the flooded freshman doorway before the gift field. Let the campus place cue create legitimate shared concern.
examples.whyItMatters: The doorway is common memory, not generic alumni pride. It makes the repair about a place that once held all of them.

examples.title: Eva Starts With the Arrival Pins

planSpec.audience: a coordinator asking attendees to share sensitive documents
planSpec.stakes: whether a shared journey cue makes trust legitimate before intake
planSpec.requiredBeat: the coordinator starts with a map pin exercise of first arrival cities before the document checklist

examples.scenario: A paper map dotted with colored pins rests beside Eva’s document checklist. Before intake, attendees mark first arrival cities and see how many routes led to the same room. Eva knows sensitive documents are next. The map pin exercise does not erase risk, but it makes shared journey visible before people decide what to place on the table.
examples.whatToDo: Begin with the arrival-city map pins before distributing the document checklist. Name the shared journey carefully and briefly.
examples.whyItMatters: The cue builds legitimate trust because the group can see a real pattern of arrival. It must support intake, not exploit vulnerability.

questions.prompt: An archivist names a street both families left behind before asking to borrow fragile letters. Which principle is active?
choices: Unity, because a real shared origin is made conscious before the trust request.
Liking, because the archivist sounds warm.
Scarcity, because the letters are fragile.
questions.explanation: The street creates a We relationship based on shared place. Warmth and fragility may matter, but they are not the central mechanism.

questions.prompt: A rural doctor shows applicants a county birth registry with their family names before discussing shifts. What makes this different from a staffing pitch?
choices: The roster becomes easier to schedule.
The registry makes place identity present before the roster appears.
The doctor avoids mentioning difficult shifts.
questions.explanation: The place cue frames the ask as service to one’s own county. It does not remove hard shifts or solve logistics.

questions.prompt: Siblings argue about boat investment. An adviser asks them to identify their grandfather’s net-mending mark before opening the budget. Why?
choices: The mark proves the engine is affordable.
The mark distracts them from conflict.
The mark makes family unity active before the capital decision.
questions.explanation: The mark brings shared inheritance to consciousness. It does not answer affordability, and distraction would avoid the decision rather than prepare it.

questions.prompt: A developer plays a child saying a clan greeting before asking elders to record pronunciations. What keeps this from becoming exploitation?
choices: The recording device is small and unobtrusive.
The greeting is a legitimate shared identity cue, and consent terms are explained plainly afterward.
The elders are praised before the form appears.
questions.explanation: Unity is clean when the identity cue is real and the request remains transparent. Device size and praise do not protect consent.

questions.prompt: An alumni appeal shows a flooded doorway everyone used as freshmen before the gift field. What does the doorway do? Before the alumni appeal is sent, the fundraiser must decide whether the flooded doorway names a real shared place or exploits nostalgia.
choices: It proves graduates can afford the donation.
It replaces the need for repair details.
It creates a campus We around a shared place.
questions.explanation: The doorway raises shared place identity. It does not establish ability to give, and repair details still have to be clear.

questions.prompt: A legal workshop begins with arrival-city map pins before asking for documents. What is the main caution? At the legal workshop sign-in table, the organizer must decide whether arrival-city pins help people feel seen or expose them.
choices: The pins should be hidden so people do not compare journeys.
The map must support real trust, not mine vulnerability for compliance.
The document checklist should be skipped.
questions.explanation: Shared journey can create unity, but sensitive intake requires care. Hiding the map or skipping documents misses the ethical issue.

questions.prompt: A manager calls employees “family” before asking for unpaid weekend work, though the workplace has high turnover. What is wrong?
choices: The word family is too emotional for any request.
Unity works only with relatives.
The We language is false and borrows intimacy the relationship has not earned.
questions.explanation: False We language exploits unity. Family cues can be legitimate in some contexts, but not when used to cover a one-sided demand.

questions.prompt: A volunteer organizer wants cooperation from neighbors after a flood. Which opening best uses place-based unity? After the flood briefing, the organizer must choose a place cue that invites neighbors into shared repair rather than borrowed intimacy.
choices: Show a map of the shared block and the houses that took water before assigning tasks.
Say everyone should be friendly and positive.
Offer a prize to the first household that signs up.
questions.explanation: The shared block is a legitimate place cue. Friendliness is not unity, and prizes use a different principle.

questions.prompt: How do you tell unity from liking? In a team debrief, the lead must decide whether the cue says we are one group or merely asks people to like the speaker.
choices: Liking depends on warmth toward a person; unity depends on a shared identity experienced as We.
Unity is just liking with stronger emotion.
Liking is ethical and unity is not.
questions.explanation: The distinction is shared identity. Unity may include liking, but it goes deeper than warmth and is not automatically unethical.

reviewCards.front: What is unity in this use of influence?
reviewCards.back: A We relationship based on shared identity, family, or place that is brought to consciousness before cooperation is requested.

reviewCards.front: Why is a shared street postmark stronger than a friendly archivist?
reviewCards.back: The postmark names a legitimate shared origin. Friendliness may help, but unity comes from being part of the same We.

reviewCards.front: When does We language become false?
reviewCards.back: When it borrows intimacy or identity that the relationship cannot honestly support, especially to smooth a one-sided request.

reviewCards.front: What does the flooded doorway do in an alumni appeal?
reviewCards.back: It brings shared campus place into awareness before the donation field, making repair feel like care for a place that held them.

reviewCards.front: What is the key question before using a unity cue?
reviewCards.back: Who has the right to name this We, and would the people inside it recognize the bond as real?

implementationPlan.coreSkill: The skill is naming a real We before asking for cooperation. You use family, origin, or place cues only when the shared identity is legitimate and the request serves that shared body.

ifThenPlans.plan: If a loan request depends on trust, then name a real shared origin before presenting the agreement.
If you ask people to serve a place, then show the legitimate place connection before the roster or schedule.
If siblings face a capital decision, then surface the shared family marker before the budget.
If shared journey can build trust, then use it briefly and keep consent terms plain.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Before one cooperation request, write the exact We you might name. If the people involved would not say it themselves, do not use it.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: This week, listen for We language in requests. Mark each one real, stretched, or false, then rewrite one stretched version into a more honest cue.

memorableLines.why: It makes the ethical weight of unity concise.

memorableLines.text: The request is not, like me.
memorableLines.why: It separates unity from ordinary liking.

memorableLines.text: Use unity only where the bond can survive being named aloud by the people inside it.
memorableLines.why: It gives the chapter’s standard for legitimate shared identity.
